Authored MIT native PE32 EXE and resource DLL. Build with `npm run build:load-images`; run Chromium acceptance with `npm run test:load-images`.

The unchanged Windows SDK client exercises both six-argument LoadImage A/W interfaces, integer/named bitmap resources, normal resource icons/cursors, requested bitmap sizes, LR_CREATEDIBSECTION, system palette flags, and BMP files through the guest filesystem. Resources and files cover indexed/CORE/monochrome/RGB24/32 and RGB565 layouts. A file with an explicit gap before its pixels verifies bfOffBits handling; missing/truncated files and invalid sizes fail. Native GetObject/GetPixel and VirtualQuery check actual bitmap handles, colors, depths and writable pointers. Pixels remain valid after the resource DLL unloads.

The window displays original resource pixels, themed resource pixels, and a top-down BMP file. F6 writes through the loaded DIB's native pointer and repaints its first pixel; press again to restore it. Chromium scans all 49,152 displayed pixels in each of three stages and requires native cleanup/exit zero. The report includes input hashes, native DLL history and browser-local x86-to-Wasm translation metrics. MinGW builds native fixture inputs on the host; their unchanged machine code is translated in the browser during execution.

The SDK client also calls SearchPathA/W to find its actual BMPs and resource DLL, then passes the returned absolute paths into LoadImage and LoadLibrary. It checks required sizes, guarded buffers, file-part pointers, extensions, explicit semicolon lists, missing/invalid names and PATH. It creates two guest directories, changes into one, verifies application-directory search after that change, loads an image while there, restores its directory and removes the temporary files/directories. Wine's native kernel32/kernelbase/ntdll code executes these searches in Chromium. Separate runtime units verify the host fallback ABI, default and safe search order, permanent safe mode, ANSI/Wide environment sharing and long/Unicode paths.

The build also produces `load-images-host.exe` for isolated host-provider units. It uses the same SDK search checks and bitmap resources, with an authored literal UTF-16 equality helper. The public GUI uses the ordinary Windows lstrcmpW import, which selects the native Wine library closure. The `--search-path-only` argument exits after the path checks; unit execution verifies actual translated native stdcall instructions and API calls without opening a GUI. Both EXEs are ordinary MinGW PE32 inputs, with no application-specific Wasm build.

**Open bitmap…** or F7 opens the standard BMP picker. Cancel preserves the image. Selecting or importing a BMP previews its full dimensions in the third panel; F6 changes/restores a physical RGB24 pixel through the native pointer. The client checks native GetCurrentDirectory after the picker and loads the selected image by its relative filename. Closing restores the original directory. Browser acceptance imports an authored BMP with reversed rows and independently checks all 16,384 preview pixels before pointer changes and after restoration. The startup SDK checks also copy a real BMP into a temporary directory, change there through native Wine, and load it relatively through USER32 before cleanup.

Bitmap sizing currently uses nearest-neighbor samples. HALFTONE filtering, compressed/embedded-image BMPs, predefined OEM bitmap assets, custom-size/file icon and cursor loading, and universal Windows compatibility remain unfinished. All image/resource data and programs are authored MIT fixtures, with no proprietary application assets.

Startup also validates the SDK four-argument GetFullPathName A/W ABI, required buffer sizes, actual file-part pointers, rooted/current-drive relative paths and in-place expansion for nonexistent bitmap names. The unchanged public executable executes native Wine paths; its host-provider variant executes the same SDK assertions against the fallback.
